page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.2-8 is a flexible compute instance powered by x86_64 AMD EPYC 9J14 processors running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The configuration allocates 4 virtual CPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores, providing 2 execution threads per core. System memory is sized at 8.0 GB of RAM, establishing a ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

This server type does not include bundled local storage or hardware GPU accelerators, requiring remote block volumes for persistent disk storage and operating system images. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because dedicated cores underpin the processing capacity, the VM offers predictable instruction throughput without resource contention from oversubscribed physical cores.

With its 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, VM.Standard.E5.Flex.2-8 aligns with compute-oriented workloads where execution tasks require moderate memory footprints. Qualitative cost efficiency is achieved by matching exact compute and memory allocations without paying for unneeded RAM or idle local disk arrays. The instance is suitable for web serving, microservices, continuous integration runners, batch data processing, and lightweight utility services.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.2-8 is a compute-focused instance powered by x86_64 AMD EPYC 9J14 processors operating at 2.3 GHz. Configured with 4 vCPUs across 2 dedicated physical cores and 8.0 GB of system memory, the VM provides a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address, while local storage is not bundled, necessitating external block storage for persistent filesystem needs. There are no GPU accelerators present. With dedicated core allocations, processing behavior remains consistent and unaffected by multi-tenant core contention. The configuration offers efficient resource balance for workloads that require modest memory per core, such as containerized services, microservices, batch processing jobs, API gateways, and web application servers.
